changes.reason: Added that Military Affairs or Chairman acting for a vacant Commander gains/loses no trophies; the Commander trophy is only when that officeholder acts.
Clarified Commanders are not officeholders and cannot be hired as Director of Trade.
Made explicit that setup follows the scenario card’s exact India political map.

answers.answer: Roll one die per held office card, adding one per fatigue and one more for the Chairman. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move the member to Pensioners, flip the office card to Vacant Offices, and return that card’s fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal attrition.

A player who retired at least one pensioner may take or discard one displayed card. Order is descending actual total retirement spending; ties go to most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. The acting player may peek at displayed blackmail. Do not replace cards during selection; if the display empties, skip remaining eligible players. Then discard all remaining display cards and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown). Return all unused pensioners to supplies.

At phase start, check whether the opportunity marker was already on the chosen main action. Take the chosen main action once, or twice if it matched; then move the marker to the chosen action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action, which is never doubled and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices, Enlist Writer gets one additional writer once this turn; a doubled Writer action therefore places three total.

After Family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt one; repeat while both remain. If Debt is gone, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order. Seek Share purchase money is paid to the bank; it does not go to Company treasuries.

Fill vacancies in ascending number on card backs. Own-family selection for ordinary offices needs verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. On promotion, transfer fatigue to the new card and insert the old card vacant in ascending order. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip it and it remains vacant, taking no actions including hiring.

The former Chairman announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half of current shares). Shareholders campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. If nobody gets that support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, with no Nepotism consent. The winner’s Company share moves to the Chairman slot and still counts for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.

Commit resources and cash first; Company-office check cash comes from that office’s treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, roll and use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds, 3–4 fails and can be retried if resources and office limits allow, 5–6 is catastrophic: no more office actions, return officeholder to supply, discard fatigue and flip card to Vacant Offices. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success. Specific Commander/firm procedures can modify this.

Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 to Balance. Each further advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares (Chairman counts); never advance past the Debt track end. Then allocate all Balance to other office treasuries, lowering Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while respecting borrowing limits; office cash already there stays available to that office.

Manager of Shipping must spend treasury cash until £2 or less remains. Lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without owner consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Place each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China if created. Extra ships return to supply at Refresh.

Declare home plus reachable regions through open orders with available ship capacity; pay £1 from the President’s treasury per die and subtract one die per declared nonhome region. On successful Trade, capacity is one order per ship in that Presidency’s sea zone (ships do not exhaust). First writer goes to home port; each later order extends the connected route filled during this Trade. Use writers then filled-order tokens as needed; writers do not limit ship capacity. Cannot fill another Presidency’s home region. At most one successful Trade per President per turn. President gets £1 per order from bank, writer owners £1 per placed writer; Company Balance gets printed order value or half rounded down where a firm already filled it this turn.

Deploy may target own Presidency’s home, an associated region, or a region bordering an associated region; not another home or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region. A Company region needs unrest or a closed order to give the action an effect. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for printed dice; subtract target plus other regions in its empire, counting target once (Company defense is zero). After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 removes that officer. Regiments do not cause officer-loss rolls.

On success, take bank loot of £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, minimum surviving participating officers in the attempt plus one for Commander. Each payout cycle pays Commander family £1 for Commander and each used surviving officer, then other families clockwise £1 per used surviving officer, then bank £1 per used regiment/alliance piece; repeat cycles until loot is gone. Commander gets one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower/dome (and all matching flags if capital), open all orders/remove unrest, place new conquest control token above associated President’s box and Governor overlay in region, Governor card only in Vacant Offices; adjust Elephant if it faced outward. Catastrophe returns half Commander family trophies rounded up and Commander to supply; exhausted officers still check losses; no card to vacate.

Governor rolls the current printed dice pool without penalty, reducing the pool by one after each attempt regardless of result. Success gives £1, or £2 if immediately preceding roll failed, then choose exactly one: build one ship stage, commission a regiment, or tax £2 to Balance or associated President treasury. A ship takes one success to place a partial ship in the region and a later success to complete it into that President’s sea zone. Regiment goes to that President’s Army. Each tax after the first this turn adds unrest. Any unsuccessful roll adds one regional unrest; catastrophe also removes the officeholder. Repeat, stop, or stop when no dice remain/catastrophe.

Expenses are £1 per Debt, officer/regiment in an Army and ship in sea zones (including China), excluding Commanders. If Balance is short, take £5 emergency loans; advance Debt only while a track space remains, and at maximum Debt keep taking loans without further advancing. Emergency Debt adds no current-turn expense; set Balance to zero after loans. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations at current Standing and lower Standing one if short. Chairman may pay affordable dividends at £1 per share, including own; if total dividend cash is strictly greater than expectations, raise Standing one.

Resolve the primary Crisis first, then secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest in Bombay, Madras, Bengal Army order; within a Presidency its Commander orders associated regions. Primary normal Crisis strength adds target unrest to normal Invasion/Rebellion strength. Foreign Invasion primary uses its ordinary attack die only, without unrest. Each secondary attack strength is only unrest cubes there. The associated Commander chooses and exhausts Army pieces; if vacant, Military Affairs acts instead; if both vacant, Chairman acts. Exhaust pieces equal to strength or as many as possible. Equal strength means attack fails and removes all attacked-region unrest. The Commander gains one trophy only when the Commander is the defense actor; Military Affairs or Chairman acting in a vacant Commander’s stead gains no trophies. If this defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove an attacker tower if possible.

answers.answer: Support −1 or less fails: discard law, resolve dilemma If Failed text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial; new PM shifts proposed policy one adjacent space and resolves that policy. Support 0 or higher passes: place law among passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve selected policy then immediate law effects. If law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.

In 1758 and Long 1710, at turn start before London Season, PM may call special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Use ordinary voting and support threshold, but there is no policy and PM may vote against it. Pass: lower Debt one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, PM takes passed-law token and activate firms. Fail: increase Company-share scoring value by Court VP token up to ±3 per share; PM remains in power and Deregulation law is not discarded. 1813 starts deregulated.

After Family share creation and before Hiring, firm investments occur until no one wants more. To form a firm, a player managing none returns an eligible Company share to supply or flips a workshop invested, flips family board to firm charter, places a member as first share, sets value cube leftmost and takes £5 from bank into London. Investment with manager consent contributes a Company share or workshop and £5 bank to London; cap ten shares, but further investments still add £5 without creating shares. Cannot use Chairman share, Company shares when Standing and/or Debt on lined space, or shares created this turn. Invested workshops never return uninvested and give neither bonus nor Company-failure VP.

Each firm gets one trade attempt per turn and needs at least one ship to select a trade strategy; may select a closed home port, but it must be open when filled. Managers secretly choose strategy/bid; bids reveal simultaneously, strategies remain facedown until matching Presidency begins. At the start of that Presidency, roll one die per £1 bid and pay bid to bank; at least one 1/2 allows trade. Initiative is ships minus successful dice; President’s successful Trade calculates same way. Lowest initiative fills first; President breaks ties, or Chairman if President is vacant/does not trade, and firms then act after Commander/Governors. Fill open orders from home route, capacity ships+1, only once per firm/order per turn; a previously filled order pays half rounded down. Each full £6 added to India treasury advances firm value one space.

At Revenue start, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus higher of share count or firm value, from either/both treasuries. If unable, dissolve unless rescued by emergency investment or negotiated merger. Dissolution sends shares to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships to matching shipyards, charter to family side; workshops remain invested. After expenses manager may dividend from India treasury only: £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. Waivers need both shareholder choice and manager consent. Record total cash actually paid on Company Balance track; active non-Hobnob paying none marks zero, Hobnob retains prior marker. Sweep remaining India money to London.

Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. Other components are limited; when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Information is public, including discards and family cash, except facedown blackmail and firm strategies/bids temporarily concealed during selection.

Negotiable: enterprises, facedown blackmail, family cash, Company/firm shares, promise cards. Not negotiable: officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial or Chairman piece. To transfer share, return old owner’s member and replace it at that share location with receiving family member; adjust VP if luxury ownership changes. Blackmail can be traded only facedown; used faceup blackmail cannot be traded.

Immediate transfers are binding; future-behavior promises are not, except guaranteed printed promise-card effect may be called if possible. Follow each card’s timing/limits and no promise calls during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which to fulfill. A promise card may be transferred to a third party or back to guarantor. A transferred resource cannot activate twice (for example, a workshop paid in Bonuses cannot pay again after sale that phase).

Use the chosen scenario’s player setup cards; add three extra cards for five players or six for six. Shuffle and deal evenly. Place every listed holding: cash and enterprise cards in family area; office members in offices and matching office cards to owners; Company-share members in Court; writers/officers/trainees in indicated boxes; Commander in Army Commander slot without office card; ships in listed sea zones or on shipyard if unfitted. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together into one deck, deal three London Season display cards (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown).

Game ends after scenario final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Failure during Events in India finishes that phase before scoring; legislation failure finishes the vote. After game end, stop negotiations, promise calls and blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use; no negotiations or promise calls during Final Scoring.

Power counts enterprises and Company shares at current track rates (bottom two positions zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for PM, and printed card power including blackmail faceup/down and applicable spouse. Most/second awards: turn 1–3 = 3/1 VP; turn 4–6 = 5/2; turn 7–8 = 8/4. Tied first each receive only lower award and no other award; tied second receive none. Highest final VP wins; tie goes to most windows, then clockwise from PM.

If Company survives, add Court’s current VP per Company share; if it fails, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. After surviving Company, roll office attrition then retire Pensioners without prestige cards. If failed, instead draw one random Company failure card. Deregulated firms score before those steps; eligible firm special retirement happens after firm scoring and before Power, whether Company survives or fails.

Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Required enterprise/share trades happen immediately on taking a spouse. Retirement discounts are personal, can stack, and each can be used once per London Season and once during Final Scoring.
A ship fitted to a returned shipyard stays in play. That shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; it becomes purchasable after the ship returns.

Enlist Writer places a family member in any Presidency Writers box; with at least four vacant offices place one additional writer once that turn. Enlist Officer places a member in Officers-in-Training. Purchase Luxury costs £4 to bank, grants luxury worth 2 VP while owned and a window icon, social enterprise. Purchase Shipyard costs £2 to bank and puts matching ship unfitted on it; shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. Purchase Workshop costs £5 to bank; manufacturing enterprise, two votes, £1 bonus, worth 1 VP on Company failure if uninvested. Seek Share costs bank £2/£3/£3/£4/£5 in queue order and places member on empty Stock Exchange space as applicant, not yet share.

If placing a family piece with none in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize’s printed VP; also applies to creating firm shares. If no Family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.

If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns as Chairman, placing a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, from a prize (lose that prize VP). If impossible, there is no Chairman.

Chairman candidates: shareholders elect. Director of Trade: Chairman picks a current officeholder other than Chairman/Governor; Commanders are not officeholders and are ineligible. If all offices are vacant, any writer is eligible. Manager of Shipping: Chairman chooses any writer. Military Affairs: Chairman chooses a Presidential Commander, else any officer, else any trainee. President: Director chooses a writer of that Presidency or a Governor associated with it. Governor: associated President chooses a writer or officer in region; Commander is ineligible. China Superintendent: Chairman chooses any writer and hires immediately on creation. Governor General replaces Director and is hired the same way. Commander appointments follow Army piece counts and are exempt from Nepotism.

Director may make repeated Special Envoy checks at £1 treasury per die, no penalty. Success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China (place overlay/card and Chairman immediately hires writer). After all envoys, Director may make up to two transfers of one writer or ship each between any Presidencies/sea zones, including China once created. Cannot transfer while still taking envoys.

Military Affairs may make up to two transfers, each an officer or regiment between Armies, remaining top half. Then place every trainee in any Army’s top half. Finally appoint Commanders: on vacancy or if a family has more total Army pieces than incumbent’s family, choose from families with most pieces; chosen officer to Commander, previous Commander to Army top as officer. Equal count does not replace incumbent. Nepotism does not apply.

Each President chooses order of its Commander, Governors and Trade; must give each position a chance, though Commander/Governors may decline. Each position completes actions before next; Trade can be ordered before/after them but cannot interrupt. If President is vacant, Chairman sets order only and cannot Trade or approve local alliance purchases.

Trade does not exhaust ships. At Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency’s Writers box, using dividers to preserve affiliation; filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply. Fitted player ships keep fatigue.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade; Upkeep and Refresh

answers.answer: At start of Commander operations, before Deploy, request President treasury funds for printed-price local alliances; President must approve. Put purchased alliance in active/top half. When used for Deploy or defense, exhaust the whole alliance to bottom. Strength usable once that turn and cannot be split among purposes. Refresh exhausts unused active alliances too; alliances do not reactivate like officers/regiments.

Company-controlled defense strength is zero, so no dice penalty from Company defense. There are no target towers and thus zero tower trophies. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, use minimum loot of surviving participating officers plus one for Commander, distributed by normal cycles. The Company region must have unrest or closed order to give the action an effect.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy — already Company-controlled region

answers.answer: Each successful Governor Build is one stage: first success places partial ship in Governor’s region; a later success completes it into the sea zone associated with Governor’s President. Governor regiments go in that President’s Army; they have officer-like strength, loot is paid to bank, and they do not roll officer-loss checks.

China is created by successful Envoy or Envoy to China law; in either case Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and Director can send ships there as to any sea zone. It acts after Bengal; China ships count Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws.

China trade is once only, including a failed attempt, so no retry; do not attempt without an export icon in Company-controlled regions. Roll one die per ship. On success, count export icons in all Company-controlled regions only: Balance gets £4 per icon; Superintendent’s family gets £1 per icon from bank. Non-Company exports do not count.

When Governor General law creates office, make all Governors pensioners, remove overlays and partially built ships, return Governor/Director cards to box. Replace Director with Governor General preserving holder and fatigue and put ribbon overlay. No new Governors/overlays upon conquest; printed Company symbols indicate control. Governor General hires Presidents, uses Director treasury/turn position, hired like Director and rolls attrition normally. Skip Governor Elimination when regions lost.

First add £3 Balance per Company region. Govern attempts cost £1 treasury per die, no penalty; every rolled 6 adds unrest to each Company region even on success. Failure adds another unrest to every Company region. Success gives £1 per Company region and requires one benefit per region: complete Company ship into any sea zone including China, put regiment in any Army, or add £2 to Balance/any office treasury except own while adding unrest to a Company region. Multiple Tax choices must put unrest in different regions. At most one successful Govern per turn.

Storms: eligible player-owned ships in affected sea zone roll once each; 1–2 nothing, 3–4 fatigue (sink if already fatigued), 5–6 sink. Sunk ship returns to shipyard unfatigued. Company and extra ships are exempt. China ships count Eastern. Firm ships count in strategy zone though on charter; Hobnob firm ships are exempt.

Return any writer on a newly closed order to owner’s supply; flip filled token to closed. If instructed to close in fully closed region, Cascade: close all open orders directly connected to its orders; if a connected order is already closed, close that region’s northernmost open order instead. If none open, it also Cascades. Region initiates a Cascade only once per event tile, but may receive effects from multiple Cascades.

Turmoil closes northernmost open order in top-stack region, Cascade if all closed. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer on orders in top-stack region and every bordering region. Shuffle: Elephant March, shuffle tile with remaining draw stack, separately shuffle discards and put them on top; if draw stack empty, March last instead.

Leader: top-stack sovereign region gains one tower. If dominated, it instead rebels using printed explosion modifier. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.

Peace on Elephant border opens orders connected across Elephant border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant wholly inside one region, instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then March in either case.

For Invasion Crisis, attacker’s whole empire strength plus event modifier must be strictly greater than defender’s whole empire strength. Success replaces defender flag with attacker’s dominated flag; taking a capital shatters its whole empire. If attacker had no empire, use free capital/star flag plus matching small flag; if none available, no new empire/flags form. Failure costs attacker one tower.

Rebellion compares only rebelling region strength plus modifier against its sovereign capital strength; other empire regions do not count. Must be strictly greater, so equal strength fails. Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes its orders (Cascade if already closed); failure removes one tower from capital.

Region Loss: Commander returns half family trophies rounded up and member to supply; roll per officer in associated Army, each 6 removes officer. Eliminate Governor (card to unused stack, fatigue/member to supply), remove overlay, partial Company ship and unrest; restore dome with one tower or Foreign Invasion specified strength and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to region with loot side down, region symbol up; region loses Presidency association. Invasion Crisis closes orders or Cascades if already closed. Standing loss is number of regions lost so far this turn (first −1, second additional −2, etc.). Other Company regions are not removed automatically; resolve their attacks/defenses separately.

After successful Invasion Crisis, Elephant moves to successful capital; after other Marches, to top-stack region. In a Company region place fully inside; dominated region points toward sovereign; sovereign points across shape-marked border on tile. If that neighbor is already dominated by actor, choose first clockwise neighbor not so dominated; if all are, use redirect-arrow shape border pointing toward empire capital.

Roll storm die for target regions: West targets Bombay, South Madras, East Bengal, all storms each, no storms top-stack region. For each, ordinary die gives attack strength and resolves Invasion/Company attack. On success close all orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove target flag and matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, set tower strength to half attack roll rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. Foreign Invasion primary attack uses die without unrest.
answers.evidence: Events — Foreign Invasion; FAQ — Foreign Invasion

answers.answer: PM draws at least one law, one at a time. After one or two ordinary (non-dilemma) draws, PM may stop or continue up to three total; choose one revealed law and discard others. Drawing a dilemma forces selection of it and ends drawing. Before voting, PM moves dial clockwise or counterclockwise to first policy space matching chosen law’s bottom icon; that space fixes target/consequence.

Tax: each family pays £1 to bank per target owned; unpaid targets return to supply, including Chairman; fitted ships remain if shipyard lost, unavailable for purchase until ship returns; prize/luxury VP is lost. Window tax additionally charges each enterprise window and each prize member window; return unpaid item. Bonus: bank pays each family £1 per owned target. Power: swap target’s marker with next higher marker; if already highest, swap any other pair.

Each £1 family cash buys one vote plus printed card votes. Each card’s votes usable once in the entire vote across rounds: rotate after use and leave rotated until vote resolves. PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes ends voting.

A supporter may later oppose; once a player opposes, cannot support during this vote. Biggest opponent holds Opposition Leader; tied current holder retains it. With recipient consent, votes may be cast for someone already opposed or committing to oppose, added to that person’s opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except forced “Vote with my enterprises” promise.

Upkeep is paid on final turn too, separately for each prize member; if unpaid, return member and lose printed VP. On nonfinal Refresh, writers return to associated Writers boxes, filled tokens/dividers and extra ships to supply, exhausted Army officers/regiments reactivate, active local alliances exhaust and do not reactivate, fitted player ships retain fatigue, then advance turn marker and begin London Season. Final turn skips Refresh and proceeds to scoring.

Each shareholder may make one additional London Season retirement from supply (not Pensioners), regardless of firms owned. Actual cash spent after spouse discounts cannot exceed highest total dividend marker among firms where they hold a share; printed prize cost can exceed marker if discounts cover difference. No retirement from firm with absent or zero marker. Spouse discounts apply normally. At Final Scoring, after firm scoring and before Power/ordinary scoring, each eligible shareholder may make one such retirement regardless of Company success/failure; no display cards.

Investment contribution takes £5 from bank into firm London treasury; trade proceeds go to India treasury. London pays ship fitting, acquisition, trade bids and expenses; India pays dividends and expenses. Remaining India cash is swept to London after dividends. Family cash cannot move into or out of firm treasuries.

Firms phase is after Family/share creation and before Hiring. Investment actions continue until nobody wants more; manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm, PM resolves conflicts between firms. Then managers secretly select strategies.

A firm can fit a ship from its own or another player’s shipyard only with that shipyard owner’s consent, paying £3 from London to bank. It may buy an already Company fleet player-owned ship with owner consent, paying Shipping treasury £3 unfatigued or £2 fatigued. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships.

Only player managing no firm may initiate hostile takeover; managing any other firm also bars it. Need consent from holders of majority target shares. Move target firm ships, money, shares to own charter and copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.

Merger requires managers’ negotiation and every shareholder’s consent. Highest-value firm is primary; tie, players choose among tied. Transfer secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards flip to family sides. Share transfers may be negotiated. If primary exceeds ten shares, with owners’ consent return excess shares to their owners’ supplies. Primary keeps its value/dividend track.
Hobnob means no bid, trade or dividends, but firm still pays expenses and retains prior dividend marker for retirement. Hobnob ships are exempt from storms.

Yes, emergency investment may still contribute when firm is at ten shares: normal Company-share/workshop contribution and £5 from bank to London, though no new share can be created over cap. Even when cap prevents shares, investment pays expenses, loses any remaining cash and lowers Value one space per emergency investment. Same-turn share restriction persists: cannot use shares created this turn even if traded away.

Emergency negotiated merger may involve only one other firm. Normal merger procedure still applies, including every involved shareholder’s consent. Other firm must pay its own expenses first if not already paid, then cover endangered firm’s unpaid expenses.

Voluntary dissolution requires consent of all shareholders. Use insolvent-firm dissolution: shares to Debtor’s Prison at −1 VP each, ships to matching shipyards, charter flips to family side. Invested workshops stay invested for rest of game and never revert.

Before ordinary final scoring, if deregulated each player totals VP from all shares in all firms and rounds that player’s total down once; subtract 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor’s Prison. Firm share rate by value: 1=−1, 2=0, 3–4=½, 5–7=1, 8–9=1½, 10=2 per share. Company failure does not change this firm-scoring step; special retirement follows it either way.
answers.evidence: Scoring — Final Scoring order; firm-track VP

answers.answer: 1710 turns 1–5, monopoly, no deregulation procedures. 1758 turns 3–7, begins with monopoly and may vote in deregulation. 1813 turns 5–8 and starts deregulated. Long 1710 turns 1–8, initial 1710 position with deregulation available.

1710: Standing expectations £10, Debt 0, each office treasury £3, Royal Protection law, one regiment per Army, no Company ships. 1758: Standing £12, Debt 3, each treasury £4, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, one Company ship East Indian, Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.

1813: Standing £10, Debt 0, each office treasury £3, Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor’s Prison side), Calico Acts; two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Put +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in Presidencies, return Governor General law to box, overlay Governor General over Director of Trade; no Governors. Scenario card reverse gives exact India towers/flags/orders/Elephant.
Final turn 1–3 gives most/second 3/1 VP; 4–6 gives 5/2; 7–8 gives 8/4. Tied first players each receive only lower award; no second award separately.
Starting Power: Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping and Manufacturing 0. Deregulation trigger: Standing £4/6/8 and Debt 5/6/7/8 are lined; Standing £4 and Debt 8 are starred. S reset is above £10.

No. Foreign Invasion primary strength is the ordinary attack die without unrest, and resulting tower strength is half that die rounded down. Successful target closes all orders; if all already closed, Cascade instead.

If Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reduces a check to zero dice, it fails. Company Fraud at start of Revenue rolls one die per your officeholder, reduces Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and receives from bank only the amount actually removed from Balance, not an overdraw. Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies. Military Oversight demotes one Commander to officer then appoints from officers; same former Commander remains eligible to become Commander again.
answers.evidence: FAQ — Applicable official errata; Company Fraud payout cap

answers.answer: Set Company Balance to £5, Power tokens to indicated starting positions, family VP markers to zero, and loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Put local alliances in named Army boxes and shuffle India events. Follow the chosen scenario setup card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and exact India political map; set Turn marker to its date and PM dial arm to the matching date.

Turn sequence: London Season, Family, Firms if deregulated, Hiring, Company Operation, Bonuses, Revenue, Events in India, Parliament Meets, Upkeep and Refresh. Eligible special Deregulation vote occurs at very start before London. Skip London Season on first game turn.

If Chairman title holder exists, they start retirements; if office vacant, former Chairman starts. Then proceed clockwise. Each player may retire each pensioner to a prize; pay printed cost, move member to prize and gain printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends for display order, then pay bank. Unused pensioners do not remain for next turn.

No. Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove surviving capital’s starred flag so it is no longer an empire. Applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest of that last dominated region.

Chairman title holder starts Family action order, then clockwise. New Company shares are processed after all players’ Family actions, moving rightmost applicants into Court while Debt remains and lowering Debt each time; with no Debt, applicants slide right while preserving order.

Red ribbon order: Chairman, Director of Trade (or Governor General), Manager of Shipping, Military Affairs, Bombay, Madras, Bengal, then China if created. Skip every vacant office; it stays vacant and takes no actions.

Roll storm die first; its face gives affected sea zones and number of India events. Resolve every required storm before drawing any event. Then draw and resolve tiles one at a time, for the indicated number. Eligible ships are player-owned ships in affected zone (China is Eastern; firm ships use strategy zone, Hobnob exempt); Company and extra ships never roll storms.

For ordinary Elephant-located Crisis, tail is attacker/acting region and head defender. Sovereign actor (large capital flag or unflagged dome) means Invasion; dominated actor (small flag or no dome) means Rebellion against sovereign. If Elephant is wholly inside Company region, it is Rebellion against Company. Foreign Invasion uses its own location rule.
